title: Frigg's Oath for Baldr
text:
Baldr, son of Odin and Frigg, was the best loved of all the gods, so fair and bright that light seemed to shine from him. One night he began to have terrible dreams that his life was in danger. When he told the other gods, they decided to protect him.

His mother Frigg traveled through all the worlds and took oaths from everything to do Baldr no harm: fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poisons and serpents. Afterward the gods made a game of it. Baldr would stand in the middle of their assembly while they threw things at him, shot arrows and struck at him with swords, and nothing hurt him.

Loki did not like this. Disguised as an old woman, he visited Frigg and asked whether everything had sworn. Frigg said yes, except a young shoot west of Valhalla called mistletoe; it seemed too young to ask. Loki went and pulled it up.

At the assembly he found Baldr's blind brother Hod standing apart. Loki gave him the mistletoe and guided his aim. Hod threw, and Baldr fell dead. The gods were struck speechless. Frigg sent a messenger to the goddess of the dead, Hel, who promised to release Baldr if everything in the world would weep for him. Everything did, except one giantess, believed to be Loki in disguise. So Baldr stayed with Hel.
lesson: No protection is total, and the small thing we overlook can matter most. Care for children by preparing them, not only by trying to shield them from everything.
people: Frigg, Baldr, Loki, Hod (Hodr), Odin, Hel
